solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drab hat's 25% off

indicators.note: a quarter taken away tells you to drop a quarter of the word's letters, here from its end

blocks.note: a wide-brimmed Mexican hat

explanation.surface: A shopper spots a dull-looking hat marked down by a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMBRERO has eight letters, so 25% is two: lose RO from the end to leave SOMBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre colours are dark and dull, so drab is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Horrible when overdrawn and current house is stripped

indicators.note: stripping something removes its outer covering, so the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: OD is the bank-statement abbreviation for overdrawn
I is the physics symbol for electric current
taken as written before stripping

explanation.surface: A bank customer finds it horrible to be in the red while their home is being emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE stripped of its outer letters leaves OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful and repellent, a close synonym of horrible.

clue.text: Have biro prepared to describe upper class manners

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
to describe can mean to draw a line around, so these letters enclose another piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
U is the standard abbreviation for upper class

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get a pen ready to write about posh etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange HAVE BIRO as BEHA-VIOR and put U inside, before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour is how one conducts oneself, which is what manners means in the plural.

clue.text: Fun space project essentially gets money allocated before Tesla

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so take its central letter
something allocated is dealt out and shared around, so these letters are redistributed

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
the middle letter of the seven-letter word
the letters to be rearranged
T is the SI symbol for the tesla, a unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A space mission's funding is allotted before Elon Musk's car company gets its share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the rearranged MONEY ahead of T. An en is a typesetting space.
explanation.definitionFit: Enjoyment is pleasure or amusement, which is what fun is as a noun.

clue.text: Accommodating invalid, fix bell by nurse's terminal

indicators.note: invalid read as not valid suggests letters in a wrong, unsound order that must be rearranged
a terminal is an end point, so take the word's last letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the final letter of nurse

explanation.surface: A helpful patient offers to repair the call bell beside the nurse's station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' poses as a sick patient, and 'terminal' as a nurse's desk or computer; both are instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible person is willing to adapt to others, which is being accommodating.

clue.text: Hide in that place briefly then advance

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the phrase's word loses its final letter

blocks.note: an animal's hide or pelt
there means in that place

explanation.surface: An instruction to lie low for a moment and then move forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to promote or push it forward, so it matches advance as a verb.

clue.text: Journalists, for example, turned up penetrating borders

indicators.note: in a down clue turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top
something penetrating goes inside another thing, so it sits within the other letters

blocks.note: EDS is short for editors
e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Reporters, as an instance, arrive having crossed frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Journalists are often shortened to editors in crosswords; the 'for example' piece is flipped and sits inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges and borders are both the outer limits or margins of something.

clue.text: Blockhead with Ian Dury irritable on tour initially

indicators.note: initially points to the beginnings, so take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone calls a fool the punk singer Ian Dury, grumpy while on a concert tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Dury was an English punk and new-wave singer, leader of the Blockheads, which makes 'Blockhead' a nice nod in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead is a stupid person, a dated synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Right to stop bias in education

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so this letter goes into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
a leaning is an inclination or bias

explanation.surface: A complaint that conservative values are needed to end prejudice in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks political in the surface, but it is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge gained through study, a near synonym of education.

clue.text: Bird has hard time trapped by inverted drink container

indicators.note: inverted means turned the other way, so the word reads backwards
being trapped means being held inside, so these letters sit within the others

blocks.note: a spirit
a jar is a container
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bird is held captive in an upturned drinks jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink container' looks like one item, but it splits into the spirit and the jar.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird with a churring call, so it is a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Beguile heart of sailor with musical instrument

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so keep only the middle letters of the word

blocks.note: the three central letters of the seven-letter word
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman's heart is won over by music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of sailor' reads as one phrase, but 'heart of' belongs to Beguile.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is a stringed instrument that is plucked or strummed, a clear example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: America's reviewed very poorly in poll

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the word goes backwards
poorly means in bad shape, so these letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: US is the United States
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An opinion poll says the US is rated very badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey and a poll are both a questioning of many people to gauge opinion.

clue.text: Wavering atheist contrived to conceal name

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged
to conceal is to hide inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A doubting unbeliever schemes to keep his identity secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ATHEIST as HESITA-T and slip N before the last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wavering is undecided and hesitant, unsure whether to act.

clue.text: Tattoo clan leader's bottom?

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is sent to the bottom, the end of the word in this down clue

blocks.note: kin are one's family or clan

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Scottish chief has a tattoo on his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the K of KIN from the top to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink someone is slang for giving them a tattoo, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Specialist, working online scam, gets £25

blocks.note: on, as a machine that is running
E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in e-commerce
a trick is a swindle
pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: An expert at internet fraud makes twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is London slang for £25, as a monkey is £500.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-trick pony is someone with only a single skill, a disparaging way to describe a narrow specialist.

clue.text: Eventful when revolutionary questioned one leaving

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-Cuban revolutionary
queried means questioned
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Things got lively when a rebel was interrogated and someone walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of QUERIED to get QUERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered history is one full of ups and downs, so eventful fits the idiom.

clue.text: Lead meeting supporting drive for baby carrier

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath the other, so it comes second

blocks.note: to push is to drive forward
to chair is to preside over a meeting

explanation.surface: A chairing role is backed up by drive to win a pram.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts CHAIR beneath PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushchair is a folding wheeled seat for a small child, a type of baby carrier.

clue.text: Fantastically enrich long day inside with kids

indicators.note: fantastically means in a wild, imaginative way, so these letters are rearranged
inside means placed within, so these letters go into the rearranged ones

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for long
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A long day spent indoors with the youngsters is wonderfully rewarding.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ENRICH as CHI-REN and put LD in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kids is the informal word for children, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Husband's skill (primarily technical) acquired by Police to make hit records

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the word's opening letter
something acquired is taken in, so these letters go inside the others

blocks.note: first part of COPPERS, slang for police
H is the abbreviation for husband
art is skill or craft
the opening letter of technical
rest of COPPERS

explanation.surface: A police team takes in a husband's technical know-how to produce bestselling singles.
explanation.walkthrough: Police are COPPERS in British slang; H, ART and T go inside it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chart-toppers are records that reached number one, which is what hit records are at their peak.

clue.text: Sound annoyed with teetotaller drinking last of Cointreau

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word
drinking means taking in, so the selected letter goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: TT, short for teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol
the final letter of the liqueur's name

explanation.surface: A non-drinker grumbles after a sip of orange liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut is to make a clicking noise of disapproval, so it means to sound annoyed.

clue.text: Mailed including information set as a basis for discussion

definitions.text: set as a basis for discussion

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the first word wraps round the letter

blocks.note: posted means sent by mail
I is the abbreviation for information, as on tourist signs

explanation.surface: Someone sent off data meant to start a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: I for information is the letter on tourist signs.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition as a premise, so posited means set out as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Tremendous pizza regularly brought into hospital unit

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter
brought into means put inside, so the selected letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A great pizza is delivered to a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Wizard as an adjective is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizard is old-fashioned British schoolboy slang for marvellous, a synonym of tremendous as praise.

clue.text: Sweet-talks more sluggish bridge partner

blocks.note: flatter means more listless or dull
South, one of the four players in bridge, partners North

explanation.surface: A card player charms their slower partner at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' here is the comparative of flat, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone is to praise them insincerely, which is what sweet-talking does.

clue.text: 'Cheers!' — no good with ordinary soft drink

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
NG is the abbreviation for no good
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A toast is spoiled when the fizzy drink served is not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'Cheers!' also means thanks, so it gives TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tango is a British brand of fizzy fruit drink, so it is an example of a soft drink.

clue.text: Spirit shot's unwise after final wine

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of the following word
an unwise move is a poorly judged one, suggesting letters put into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the final letter of wine
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shot of spirits after the last glass of wine is a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a drink in this boozy surface, but it means character.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethos of a group is its characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs.

clue.text: Old city church's home for street kid

blocks.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
CH is the abbreviation for church
in means at home

explanation.surface: A historic church in the old town provides a shelter for homeless children.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, poor child who roams the streets.

clue.text: Some in club ran charitable section

indicators.note: some of what is in the phrase means only part of its letters are taken, running across the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of club, all of ran and the start of charitable

explanation.surface: A few members of a society organised its charity arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a division or section of an organisation.

clue.text: Reject routine that's backfired, producing a yawn

indicators.note: something that has backfired has gone the wrong way, so the word is read backwards
producing suggests making something new out of the given letters, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: a rut is a dull routine
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boring act that went wrong only drew yawns, so it was rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing a yawn' reads as boredom, but the yawn supplies letters to rearrange after the turned-round routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn away someone is to refuse them entry or help, which is to reject them.

clue.text: Authorised staff to return in dense fog

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start
to fog is to confuse or blur, so these letters are jumbled
in places the first piece inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a rod is a staff or stick
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Employees were given permission to come back in thick fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fog' looks like the noun the dense describes, but it is a verb telling you to jumble dense.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to approve or sanction it, so endorsed means authorised.

clue.text: Mock fancy eiderdown at first

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorated, suggesting the letters are worked into a new form
at first keeps only the opening letter of the second half of the word, so the rest of that half is dropped

blocks.note: the quilt, read as two halves: eider kept whole, and down of which only the opening letter stays

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a showy quilt at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits eiderdown in two: eider is kept whole and down keeps only its first letter, then those six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule or scorn, which is what mock means as a verb.
